old_title: Berlin Pride attack latest: Police hunt suspect, 21, after one killed in attack
new_title: Manhunt for suspect, 21, after Berlin Pride crowd struck in 'Islamist terror attack'
old_text:
One person died and at least 16 others were injured after a car drove into a crowd during Berlin's LGBTQ+ parade on Saturday evening.
Berlin fire brigade said that three of the victims were in life-threatening condition, while eight were in serious condition, per Sky News.
A suspect in the Berlin attack was identified in the early hours of Sunday morning as a member of the city's "Islamist scene", according to police. Police and prosecutors asked for help in finding the 21-year-old, whom they identified as Abdul B.
"We have now identified a suspected perpetrator. Measures against this suspected perpetrator, who has not yet been arrested, are underway. However, this suspected perpetrator is known to the police as a member of the Islamist scene here in Berlin," said the spokesperson.
According to police, a car had driven into the Tiergarten park, near the route of the pride march, hitting several people.
Hundreds of thousands of people had come to Berlin on Saturday to celebrate at Berlin's pride parade, known in Germany as Christopher Street Day. It's one of Europe's largest LGBTQ+ celebrations.
Police name 21-year-old suspect in Berlin Pride attack
German authorities on Sunday issued a wanted notice for a fugitive suspect in the van ramming near Berlin's Pride festival that left one person dead and injured at least 16 others.
Police and prosecutors asked for help in finding the 21-year-old, whom they identified as Abdul B.
They said he is believed to have injured several people with a moving vehicle, and that one or more people apparently then left that vehicle. Several people were also apparently stabbed, they added.
Sunday's notice warned the public to avoid "direct contact" with the suspect, saying that he may be armed and dangerous.
Police had said earlier that they had identified a suspect who has ties to Islamic groups in the German capital."The suspect is known to police. He is known to us as a member of Islamic circles here in Berlin, and our search for this person is proceeding at full speed," police spokesperson Florian Nath said.
Nath added that "we still have no information whatsoever regarding his specific motives, the exact sequence of events, or his role in the crime itself."
Wes Streeting: 'Horrific' attack shows why Pride marches are important
Britain's defence secretary Wes Streeting has described the attack in Berlin as an "absolutely horrific disaster".
Discussing Pride marches, he told Sky's Sunday Morning with Trevor Phillips: "In many respects, things are different and better now than they've ever been... But hate crimes are also on the rise. There are lots of people who don't accept diversity and difference in our society.
"And that's why pride is a celebration. But it's also a protest against those who do not accept life in the 21st century, do not accept people loving each other in same-sex relationships and in the very worst cases would seek to do us harm."
Asked about safety at next week's annual Brighton Pride celebrations, he said "these types of events are always well policed".
RECAP: Manhunt for Berlin Pride attack suspect who may be 'armed and dangerous'
- Police in Germany are hunting for a man suspected of ramming a van into a crowd at an LGBTQ+ parade in Berlin on Saturday evening, with several people also reportedly stabbed
- One person died and at least 16 others were injured. Berlin fire brigade said that three of the victims were in life-threatening condition, while eight were in serious condition
- Police have released a picture of the suspect, who they have identified as 21-year-old Abdul B, but warned the public he may be armed and dangerous
- Chancellor Friedrich Merz described the incident as an "attack on our society" as police said the investigation is continuing at "full speed"
'Tolerant and peaceful' Berlin was attacked in most 'brutal way', mayor says
The mayor of Berlin, Kai Wegner, said the "brutal" incident was "an attack on our free and open society" and the "tolerant and peaceful" city.
In a post on X, he said: "Berlin is the city of freedom - and our freedom has been attacked in the most horrific way today. My thoughts are with the victims, their families and friends.
"I thank the emergency services who were immediately on site and did everything in their power. And I trust the police and security authorities, who will investigate at full speed."
Incident was an 'attack on our society', Merz says
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz described what happened as "an attack on our society."
"What an abhorrent act in Berlin," Merz wrote in a post on X. He added that Germany loves freedom, "and we will preserve and defend that."
Hundreds of thousands of people had come to Berlin on Saturday to celebrate at Berlin's pride parade, known in Germany as Christopher Street Day.
Photo released of suspect identified as Abdul B
Police have identified a 21-year-old suspect called Abdul B in connection with the incident.
He is described as slim build, approximately 1.90 m tall, black hair, black hoodie and white pants.
Several people suffering from 'life-threatening' injuries, say police
Berlin police report that one person has been killed and 17 people injured following a ramming incident at a Pride event on Saturday evening.
This includes "several with life-threatening injuries", according to police.
new_text:
Police have captured and shot dead the man suspected of killing a woman and injuring 29 others at a Pride event in Berlin in what authorities believe was an Islamist terror attack.
The attacker, named as Abdul Ballout, a 21-year-old German citizen with Lebanese roots, was found at an allotment site in the Spandau area of the city on Sunday evening almost 24 hours after the car and machete rampage.
Berlin police said he ran at emergency services personnel with a "stabbing weapon", before armed officers fatally shot him.
Three victims were still fighting for their lives in hospital on Sunday after sustaining life-threatening injuries, and eight others were seriously injured in the attack.
Police believe Ballout drove into crowds in the Tiergarten park near the Brandenburg Gate at about 8pm on Saturday. He then got out of the car and lashed out at victims with the blade.
His death ended a manhunt in which residents were warned Ballout he may be armed and dangerous.
"Everything we see here points to us dealing with an Islamic terror attack," interior minister Alexander Dobrindt said earlier, adding that the suspect had "drawn attention to himself through a high volume of criminal offences, radicalisation and affiliation with the Islamist scene".
He was previously sentenced to one year and 10 months in prison, which was later suspended.
Victims were a mix of festival goers and other locals in the park, which is a few hundred metres from the Christopher Street Day parade closing party at Brandenburg gate.
Hundreds of thousands of people had come to Berlin to celebrate at the Pride parade, which is one of Europe's largest LGBTQ+ celebrations.
The celebration was abruptly called off around 10:15pm and a band's performance on stage was interrupted as people were urged to go home and to avoid taking the route through the park.
As crowds gathered for a vigil at St Mary's Church in Berlin on Sunday, German chancellor Friedrich Merz urged those celebrating at Pride events not to be intimidated.
"I would like to say this to Christopher Street Day participants here in Berlin but also across Germany: Don't let yourselves, let us not let ourselves be intimidated," he said.
"These acts have only one purpose: They aim to divide our society. They want to take away from us the most important thing we have: Namely our openness and our freedom."
He said officials will do everything in their power to catch the perpetrator.
Alexander Dobrindt, the interior minister, promised to review security measures at other major events in Germany, including Pride events elsewhere, admitting they cannot rule out copycat attacks. He said: "This is not typical of such situations, but it also can't be ruled out."
There were emotional scenes as festival goers gathered at Brandenburg gate on Sunday for an impromptu protest, leaving flowers and paying tribute to victims of the attack. One sign, left with a bouquet of flowers at the park read simply: "Love wins."
Defence secretary Wes Streeting joined other world politicians in condemning the "absolutely horrific" incident. The cabinet minister suggested the attack showed why such LGBTQ+ events were still necessary.
He told Sky News' Sunday Morning with Trevor Phillips: "There are lots of people who I think don't accept diversity and difference in our society, and that's why pride is a celebration but it's also a protest against those who do not accept life in the 21st century, do not accept people loving each other in same-sex relationships, and in the very worst cases, would seek to do us harm."
The attack came a week before Britain's biggest Pride festival is due to take place in Brighton and Hove.
Mr Streeting said: "The home secretary will obviously, with police chiefs, make the right determinations around what kind of policing presence we need."
Organisers of Brighton and Hove Pride joined other LGBTQ+ groups in an outpouring of support following the attack. "This is why we march for our rights," they said in a post on social media. "Pride should be a place of celebration and joy. Brighton stands with Berlin."
Pride in London said their "hearts are broken" by news of the Berlin attack, adding: "Pride is a movement built on community, courage and solidarity. In moments of unimaginable pain, we come together. We remember why we march, why we speak out and why we stand with one another."
Manchester Village Pride said it was "deeply saddened" by the events and sent "love, strength, and unwavering support" to the Berlin Pride community.
"Pride is a celebration of love, diversity, inclusion, and the freedom to be who you are. When one Pride community is impacted, we all stand together in solidarity," they added.
